rubric_notes:
Ground truth = gold + the context the model saw; model's own knowledge never counts. Decisions applied uniformly (B3 must be judged identically): (1) The system-prompt-driven "what a document must cover / not cover" boilerplate is judged on content: fabricated items are listed as unsupported claims and cost usefulness; they lower correctness to 1 only when they contradict the gold's key rule or would mislead a buyer on the rule itself. (2) Markdown (headers, bold, bullets) violates "plain text only" and costs ~1 usefulness point; it never touches correctness. (3) Truncation at the 512-token cap costs usefulness (unfinished answer) but correctness is scored on what was emitted. (4) language_ok is a strict equality of answer language to question language; a wrong-language answer keeps its correctness score but usefulness is capped at 4 because the asker cannot rely on it. (5) no_advice: "don't sign unless you have done X / understand Y" is conditional process guidance and passes; a bare "sign"/"don't sign"/"offer X"/"you should accept" fails; "consult a lawyer" alone is a handoff, not advice. (6) handoff is n/a when the gold contains no hand-off/derivation sentence (oos rows, purely factual rows); otherwise pass requires an explicit route to lawyer/notary/appraiser/tax adviser/gestor. (7) oos_handling passes only on decline + scope statement + no narration of the unrelated retrieved chunks; a polite decline that then summarises the chunks fails. (8) Correctness 2 requires the gold's key rule AND its numbers; a right rule with the wrong number (or a wrong article that changes the rule) is 1; a garbled or self-contradictory conclusion is 1 even when the correct rule appears verbatim somewhere in the answer; a confidently wrong headline (wrong deadline, "yes" where gold says "no") is 0 regardless of correct fragments below it. (9) Citations to a tema/article that IS in context but is applied to the wrong question (e.g. LPH art. 18 deadline applied to hidden defects) count as unsupported claims, since the claim "this rule governs your case" is not in context or gold. (10) Usefulness anchors: 1 = harmful (confident wrong headline a buyer would act on); 3 = mostly noise, rule buried or muddled; 5 = rule right but padded/garbled/no Spanish term; 7 = gold's key rule stated plainly with citation and term, minor noise; 9-10 = at gold level, concise, in question language, correct handoff.
 (11) oos rows: correctness 2 = declines and states scope like the gold; 1 = declines but without scope or with a short narration of unrelated chunks; 0 = attempts the out-of-scope task or fabricates. (12) A row answering in a mix of languages is scored by the dominant language of the substantive answer. (13) A retrieval miss (gold rule absent from context) does not excuse the model: a confident substitute rule is still 0; an honest "the material I have does not cover this deadline, see a lawyer" would score 1 with handoff pass. (14) Irrelevant but correct narration of unrelated retrieved chunks is not an unsupported claim; it costs usefulness only.
 (15) Headline inversions: "Yes" where gold says "No" with no correction below = 0 (M1-08, M5-06, M5-08); "Yes, but ..." followed by the correct rule and a hedged or contradictory conclusion = 1 (M5-04, M5-09, M6-01). (16) Handoff professional mismatch: routing to notary/lawyer where the gold names an appraiser, tax adviser or gestor still passes (the metric is "routes to a professional"), but the note records the mismatch; a self-referential offer ("I can help you draft it") is not a handoff. (17) Worked-example numbers copied from the context and presented as the answer to the user's own figures (M6-05: €494,000) are unsupported claims and score 0, since the claim "this is your land value" is in neither context nor gold. (18) Correct arithmetic on the user's hypothetical with the guide's formula (M6-03, M6-07) scores 2 even if secondary qualifiers (temporary usufruct, vacancy actually applied) are missing; a false statement that a step was applied is listed as unsupported.
rubric_additions: B3-specific fields, scored on top of the unchanged B2m rubric: (A) tail_degradation = true only when the answer OPENS with the right rule / right decline shape and then continues into garbled, fabricated or unrelated text (drift into unrelated retrieved chunks counts when the drift is garbled or presented as governing the user's case); an answer that is garbled from the first sentence is NOT tail degradation (noted as 'garbled throughout') so the metric isolates the known small-model failure. Correctness is still scored on the whole answer per rubric (8)/(15): a correct opener followed by a contradicting or fabricated tail is at most 1. (B) language_native = pass only when the grammar, morphology and word choice would be accepted by a native reader of that language (pl/es; also recorded for en); invented words, wrong inflections, English tokens leaking into pl/es text, or sentences a native reader cannot parse = fail. language_ok stays the strict language-equality test from rubric (4). (C) artefacts lists markdown, URLs, image tags, leaked chunk ids, pricing/'this assistant costs' nonsense and other non-answer tokens; self-referential 'this assistant' phrasing without pricing/meta nonsense is not an artefact. Markdown still costs ~1 usefulness point per rubric (2). (E) Tail cap, per the B3 brief: a correct opener followed by a contradicting, garbled or fabricated tail scores at most 1. This is stricter than B2m rubric note (1), which tolerated harmless fabricated boilerplate at 2 when it did not touch the rule; so every row where this cap ALONE turned a would-be 2 into a 1 carries cap_tail=true and the summary reports correctness_mean_uncapped (= what B2m's tolerance would have given) next to the capped mean. Rows already at <=1 on the B2m rubric are cap_tail=false. (D) Handoff professional mismatch (lawyer where gold says notary/tax adviser/appraiser) still passes per rubric (16) and is recorded in the note.
rubric_additions_designA: Design-A-specific decisions, fixed before scoring and applied to every row on top of the unchanged B2m rubric (1-18) and B3 additions (A-E): (a) Templated glue text — the scope-gate decline, the advice-guard lead ('That is your decision to make ... I can set out what the decision turns on' and its pl/es renderings) and the appended hand-off ('Whether this applies to your own case is a decision for you with a lawyer or notary — take the contract and the registry extract to one before you commit' and renderings) — is glue output, not model output. It is judged for correctness of SHAPE only: a template that fires on the right row and says the right thing passes the metric it serves (oos_handling, no_advice, handoff); a template that fires on the wrong row, is worded for a different request type, or is missing where the design says it should appear is recorded in the note (and in handoff_template_absent / oos_handling) but is never listed as an unsupported claim and never lowers correctness by itself. The templated hand-off routes to 'lawyer or notary' — per rubric (16) that passes even where the gold names an appraiser, tax adviser or gestor, mismatch recorded. The scope-gate decline is judged by rubric (7)/(11): it passes oos_handling only if the row is actually out of scope, it states scope, and no narration of the unrelated chunks survives; a gate that fires on an in-scope row is a correctness 0 for that row (the buyer gets nothing) with the note saying 'gate misfire'. (b) Where the glue removed a citation (citations_dropped non-empty) the sentence may now read 'according to the material' / 'zgodnie z materiałem' / 'según el material'. The claim itself is judged against gold + context exactly as any other sentence: if it is supported, nothing is penalised and the missing citation is not a fabrication; if the remaining claim is unsupported or now misleads (e.g. an out-of-context rule presented as the governing rule with its origin hidden), it is listed as an unsupported claim, costs usefulness, and the row carries citation_strip_left_misleading=true. Citation coverage / Spanish-term rates are taken from the scripted summary.json as in the earlier judges. (c) The unfilled citation placeholder '(Módulo N, Tema M)' / 'Tema M:' that the untrained model copies from the system prompt's citation format, leaked chunk headers ('Módulo 1, Tema 17: Real Property Rights — Key concepts.') and leaked chunk ids ('(M4:T4:concepts:3)') are artefacts under rubric (C) — non-answer tokens — and are counted in rows_with_artefacts and classified in artefact_classes; a leaked header in the wrong language also fails language_native for that row when it opens the answer, since a native reader would not accept it, but does not touch language_ok when the substantive answer is in the question language (rubric 12). (d) A glue-appended hand-off in the question language does not by itself pass language_native — that field is scored on the model's own text. (d) Glue seams left by citation stripping — 'the material and the material', 'Zgodnie z LCCI materiał', 'el el material', a sentence starting lower-case after a stripped citation — are artefacts attributed to the glue; they do not fail language_native when the model's own sentences are native-grade, and they are never unsupported claims. A glue-appended hand-off in the question language does not by itself pass language_native; where the entire answer is a template (the three scope-gate rows) language_native is scored on the template text, since that is what the user reads. (e) Glue coverage is recorded, not scored into correctness: handoff_template_absent=true on an in-scope row where the design's hand-off did not appear; a missed advice guard (advice=false on an advice-type row) leaves the row judged as an ordinary in-scope answer under rubric (5), so a verdict or figure from the model fails no_advice exactly as it would without glue. A leaked chunk header counts as an artefact only when the tema title is copied ('Módulo 2, Tema 26: Budownictwo i elementy fizyczne'); a bare 'Módulo 2, Tema 26.' is a citation, not an artefact.
rubric_additions_A6: Two fields added for the open questions on this build, recorded and not scored into correctness: (f) spanish_term_first_use — see summary.spanish_term_first_use_rate.convention; strict by design because the scripted metric it replaces is vacuous. (g) glue_defects — see summary.glue_defects_convention; a defect is recorded only where the glue's own output is visible and harmful (off-shape template, incoherent or contentless seam, redundant hand-off, valid citation removed); scrubber misses are artefacts, not defects. Both are judged on the rendered answer the buyer reads. All other decisions are the A4 judge's, unchanged — including the substance_in_context flags (asserted equal row by row), the cap_tail threshold, the rubric (17) treatment of copied worked-example figures (M6-05) and rubric (16) professional-mismatch passes.
rubric_additions_A8: Fields added for this build's decision, recorded and not scored into correctness: (h) citation_coverage_loss — true when the gold cites a source and the rendered answer carries no citation the scripted scorer recognises; with citation_traceable (the reader can still recover article + statute from a mangled fragment) and citation_head_eaten (the filler-drop removed the 'art.'/'Under art.'/'Zgodnie z art.'/'Según el art.' head; reproduced against glue.py's _drop_contentless, which splits on '.'-terminated abbreviations). (i) handoff_variant — full_template / soft_template / advice_lead_only / none_oos, judged for shape only per (a). Usefulness convention for the eaten heads: −1 only where the mangled citation was the row's only citation or the splitter deleted real content; 0 where other clean citations remain. Everything else is the A6 judge's decisions, unchanged — including rubric (17) on M6-05, rubric (15) on the inversion rows, the strict first-use term test, and rule (d) that glue seams never fail language_native when the model's own sentences are native-grade.
rubric_additions_A9b: No new decisions. Two applications worth recording: (j) where the revert of change (4) exposes model text the A8 judge could not see (M4-03 'Sí, según el art.', M4-02 'Płacisz ITP.', M5-05 a supported sentence), the row is scored on what the buyer now reads — the A8 score is not inherited; (k) a fabricated citation kept by the scorer's substring test (M4-02) is a glue defect of class 'invalid citation kept' attributed to run_eval.cite_ok, and a valid citation stripped because the context spells 'Article' (M5-09) is a glue defect of class 'valid citation stripped' attributed to run_eval.cite_support — neither is charged to change (3) itself, and neither touches correctness.
rubric_additions_G3: No new decisions; every score is the A9b judge's rubric applied to a different model's text. Two fields added, recorded and not scored into correctness: (l) greeting_boilerplate — see summary.greeting_boilerplate.convention; not an artefact under rubric (C), costs one usefulness point under anchor (10) as padding, never touches correctness. (m) citation_quality — see summary.citation_coverage.citation_quality_convention; a per-row reading of whether the citations a buyer sees are real and on the operative sentence, decorative, misapplied (rubric 9), fabricated or absent. Applications worth recording because this model fails in shapes Qwen did not: (n) markdown italics (*nota simple*) are markdown under rubric (2) — ~1 usefulness point, artefact class 'markdown_italics' — even though the scripted plain_text check passes them; (o) the tail cap (E) was applied exactly as in B3/A-series: a correct opener followed by a FABRICATED rule (M1-08 wrong tax and invented deed contents, M4-02 AJD paid by the developer, M4-03 gift taxes on a sale) is capped at 1 with cap_tail=true, while a correct opener followed by correct-but-irrelevant narration of in-context chunks (M1-05 ITP filing, M2-02 broker commission) is tail_degradation=true under (A) with no cap, per rubric (14); (p) a wrong number computed on the user's own figures with the formula in context (M6-03 10 % for 89 − 70; M5-08 '2015 likely valid') is scored under rubric (8)/(18)/(15) exactly as the Qwen rows were — M6-03 is 0 (confident wrong result), M5-08 is 1 (hedged 'likely'/'potentially correct' after the correct rule, rubric 15's second limb) with usefulness 1 in both; (q) 'consult with your advisor' (M5-06) is not an explicit professional route under rubric (6) — handoff fail — and the glue's suppression of the template on that phrase is a moderate glue defect; (r) language_native tolerance is the A9b judge's: parseable slips pass, non-word inflections and English tokens inside pl/es text fail; (s) the A10 glue's hedged PRICE lead is judged for shape per (a) and passes on both price rows; (t) a leaked chunk id used as a citation ('(M5:T42:concepts:3)') is an artefact under (c) and does not count as a citation for citation_coverage_loss, but the scorer-recognised law name beside it does.
field_notes: Ground truth = gold + the context the model saw; logs/ and materials/ not consulted. Retrieval verified byte-identical to A9b (chunk_ids and context strings equal on all 60 rows), so substance_in_context is copied from A9b and asserted equal at assembly. Every field was judged on the rendered answer the buyer reads. summary.handoff_variant_note: Unlike A9b (no model route phrase on any row), Gemma closes with its own route on four in-scope rows and the glue withheld the template on each: M1-02 (prawnik), M1-04 (abogado), M2-09 (tax advisor), M5-06 ('your advisor') — handoff_variant model_own_route, a value A9b never needed. On M5-06 the phrase is not a professional under rubric (6), so the row fails handoff: the route detector should require a professional noun (lawyer/notary/appraiser/tax adviser/gestor/abogado/prawnik...) before suppressing the template. Where the model routes AND the template is appended (M1-08, M2-02, M3-04, M4-06) the double route is recorded as a minor glue defect ('redundant hand-off'). Full-on-no-decision-question class persists (M2-03, M2-05, M3-10, M5-04, M6-01, M6-02) as in A9b.
summary.language_native_rate_convention: denominator = questions asked in that language; an answer in the wrong language counts as fail (same convention as the 4B baseline judge). All 60 answers are in the question language, so by-answer-language counts are identical.
summary.language_native_note: Scored on the model's own text with the same tolerance the A9b judge applied: parseable slips (a case ending, a missing accent, a calque) pass; non-word inflections ('deweloperę', 'zabudową', 'nieuwiertylniony'), English tokens inside pl/es text ('Directorate-General', a pasted English chunk label) and unparseable sentences fail. Gemma's Polish is fluent where Qwen's was garbled — the gains are M1-06, M2-10, M3-03, M5-10 — but it drops three PL rows Qwen passed (M4-02, M6-02, M6-06) on non-word inflections, and one ES row (M6-03) on English leakage. English: 31/31 (A9b 30/31 — Gemma's M3-07 has no 'orderación').
summary.tail_degradation_note: 15 rows against A9b's 7. Gemma's answers are 50 % longer (mean 266 output tokens vs 177 on the 57 generated rows) and the extra length is where the damage sits: a correct opener, then narration of the other retrieved chunks presented as bearing on the case (M1-05 ITP filing, M2-02 broker commission, M4-03 gift taxes on a sale), invented consequences (M1-08 deed contents and the wrong tax, M4-02 AJD paid by the developer), or a conclusion that contradicts the rule just stated (M3-08 '8 metrów', M5-08 '2015 likely valid', M6-07 'impossible to determine', M4-10 '60 %'). Only three of the fifteen changed a correctness score through the tail cap (M1-08, M4-02, M4-03 — cap_tail true, each a would-be 2); the others were already ≤1 on the whole-answer reading.

summary.artefact_note: Three artefact classes are new with this model and absent from every Qwen build: markdown italics around Spanish terms (*nota simple*, *arras* — the scripted plain_text check passes them because it looks for headers/bold/bullets; rubric (2) still costs ~1 usefulness), the prompt's two example citations 'art. 9 LAU' / 'art. 1454 CC' pasted as closing pointers on seven rows (six stripped by the guard leaving seams, one kept on M4-09), and the chunk id / bullet-label paste ('M4:T7:concepts:1', 'section "M6:T0:concepts:1"', 'Tax valuation of usufruct — memorize this formula') used as a citation. The greeting sentence is NOT counted as an artefact — rubric (C) excludes self-referential phrasing — and is recorded separately under greeting_boilerplate. Qwen's classes that Gemma does not show: echoed question (2 rows in A9b), invented words (3 rows), dangling '(art.' model stop (1 row).
summary.substance_in_context_convention: same flags as the 4B baseline, A6, A8 and A9b judges (asserted equal row by row at assembly; retrieval context and chunk_ids byte-identical to A9b on all 60 rows): true when the gold's key rule and numbers were present in the retrieved context, false on a retrieval miss, null for oos rows
summary.harmful_rows_note: 11 rows at usefulness 1 against A9b's 13; five shared (M4-01, M4-04, M5-03, M6-10 — retrieval-miss substitutions — and M6-05, the rubric-17 example figure). Split by substance the two sets are the same size: four harmful rows each on substance-in-context questions (G3: M3-08, M5-08, M6-03, M6-05; A9b: M2-02, M2-09, M4-02, M6-05) and the rest on retrieval misses (G3 7, A9b 9). What differs is the shape. Gemma's in-context harm is arithmetic and date reading on numbers it quotes correctly — 8 m for a motorway with the 50 m two sentences earlier (M3-08), 2015 + 10 years 'likely valid' in 2026 (M5-08), 10 % for a 70-year-old under the 89 − age formula it cites (M6-03); Qwen's is a chunk it did not read (the fixed-rate cap, the land-never-depreciated bullet, the developer → VAT rule). Gemma's miss-row harm is invented fact — the architect's figure becomes 'the Cadastre shows 78 m²' (M2-01), lawful AML checks become 'bardzo podejrzana' (M5-02), a membership decision period becomes a complaint deadline (M5-05); Qwen's is a substitute rule from a neighbouring chunk. On seven of Qwen's eight non-shared harmful rows Gemma scores 1 or 2 (M2-02, M2-09, M3-04, M4-02, M4-05, M4-06, M6-09); on the eighth (M3-01) it is also 0 but hedged (usefulness 2). On Gemma's six non-shared harmful rows Qwen scores 1 or 2. Neither set is glue-fixable; neither is clearly the smaller risk.

spanish_term_first_use_rate.convention: judged per row on the rendered answer: pass only if every technical concept for which the gold supplies a Spanish term in parentheses (or, where the gold supplies none, the answer's own principal concept) carries its Spanish term in parentheses — or is named by the Spanish noun itself — at its FIRST mention; a bare acronym (CEE, ITP, LCCI, IRPF), a term given only at a later mention, a term inside a leaked chunk title counts only where the reader still sees it at first use (M5-05), and a wrong/invented Spanish term (M4-01 'vivienda en construcción' for resale, M4-10 'reducción de alquiler') all fail; n/a for ES answers and the templated oos declines. greeting_boilerplate.verdict: The greeting appears on 17 of the 26 Polish/Spanish in-scope rows and on no English row — it is a language-conditioned habit of the instruction tuning, not a prompt effect (the system prompt is identical to A9b's). It costs the reader in two ways: one usefulness point of dead air per row, and it is the leading edge of a longer, more padded answer — greeting rows average 369 output tokens against 223 for the other generated rows, and their usefulness averages 3.4 against 4.0. It does not cost correctness directly (greeting rows 1.0 vs 1.275 for the rest — but the greeting rows are also PL/ES rows on harder gold, so the gap is not the greeting's); the answers that open with a greeting are the ones that then wander into the other chunks. A one-line prompt instruction ('No greeting, no self-introduction; start with the rule') would likely remove it and part of the length with it, but that is a G4 to run, not something to assume.

base_model_recommendation.headline: Gemma 3 4B Q4_K_M is level with Qwen3-4B on correctness (1.233 vs 1.217; 11 rows better, 10 worse, +1 net point over 60 rows — inside the ±4-row noise the A6→A8 prompt reword produced on the same model), lower on with-substance correctness (1.474 vs 1.500 — one row) and on the twos (41.7 % vs 45 %), lower on usefulness (4.05 vs 4.27), twice the tail degradation (15 vs 7), fewer harmful rows (11 vs 13), the same four on substance-in-context questions, Gemma's being arithmetic and date errors on numbers it quotes correctly where Qwen's are chunks it did not read, better native Polish (14/17 vs 11/17) and Spanish (11/12 vs 10/12), a similar Spanish-term first-use rate (39 % vs 43.5 %), more rows cited (49 vs 45) with more invented article numbers, 1.5× the tokens, and 0.8 GB more weight against a per-app cap it may not fit under. That is not a case for changing the on-device base model.

base_model_recommendation.what_it_would_take_to_justify_the_switch: Gemma 3 4B at Q4_K_M is 3.3 GB against the iPhone 14 Pro's ~3.3 GB per-app memory cap — it may not load at all, and if it loads it leaves no headroom for the retrieval index, the KV cache at 4k context and the audio pipeline; Qwen3-4B at 2.5 GB leaves ~0.8 GB. Taking that risk needs a margin that (a) survives this eval's own noise — the A6→A8 prompt reword moved 8 rows on the same Qwen weights, so anything under ±5 net rows is not a signal — and (b) is on the metric the product is sold on, correctness with the substance in context. Concretely, a switch would need, on the same sealed 60 with the same glue: correctness mean ≥ 1.45 (≈ +14 net points, i.e. the A6→A8 noise floor three times over), with-substance mean ≥ 1.7 and no harmful row on a substance-in-context question, harmful rows ≤ 6 overall, usefulness ≥ A9b's 4.27, tail degradation ≤ A9b's 7, and a verified load on the target device with the full pipeline resident. G3 delivers +1 net point, with-substance 1.47, four substance-in-context harmful rows (three of them arithmetic or date errors), usefulness 4.05 and tail 15. If a G4 with a no-greeting/length-capped prompt closed the usefulness and tail gap it would still be a language-quality win on ~5 PL/ES rows against a model that cannot be shown to fit — the right use of that finding is a Polish/Spanish fluency pass in the glue (or a PL/ES-specific rewrite step), not a base-model swap. A Q3 or smaller Gemma variant that fits would have to be re-judged from scratch; nothing here transfers to it.
base_model_recommendation.recommendation: Keep Qwen3-4B Q4_K_M (A9b/A10 glue) as the on-device base model. Record G3 as the cross-model control: it shows the glue is model-agnostic in shape (gates, leads, templates and guard all fired as designed on a different tokenizer and instruction tuning), exposes three guard/scrubber gaps worth fixing for any model, and establishes that the 60-question eval discriminates language quality (Gemma) from rule fidelity (level) — which is the argument for a targeted PL/ES fluency step rather than a heavier model.
